newsitem.title: HUNGARY: JAPANESE RATE HIKE FEARS FADE, PULL YEN LOWER.
newsitem.headline: JAPANESE RATE HIKE FEARS FADE, PULL YEN LOWER.

text.p: Falling yen futures and the launch of Czech crown featured modest activity on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE)'s currency futures section on Thursday.
"The possible rate hike in Japan seems unlikely to materialise in the near future," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.

Futures for yen -- the day's most actively traded contract -- closed lower for all maturities, losing by between 2.50 and 3.21 forints. Of the day's 18,129 currency contracts, worth 2.96 billion forints, 11,175 were for the yen.
The BCE launched trading in Czech crown, increasing the number of currency futures to eight, but the first day saw no deals.
"Market maker banks had some difficulties, they could not calculate futures prices as they do not have access to appropriate information about Czech crown interest rates," Otvos said.
"I can imagine this situation to last for a week."
Short-sellings pushed the Czech crown to record lows last week, prompting the Czech central bank to intervene.
Elsewhere on the market, the dollar was stronger for all maturities and the mark firmed for December, the only traded maturity. December mark edged up 11 fillers to 116.51 in 1,750 contracts.
